lines.en: It’s been just under twenty-four hours since I rode the ferris wheel again.
And to think I almost didn’t pick up the phone.
It isn’t often that Tsuneyo’s name pops up on the screen, so I assumed she was just dialing my number on accident at first.
But, for whatever reason (whether that reason be fate or luck or anything in between), I did. And I must now deal with the consequences.
And the reason I say that like it’s a bad thing is because, right now, it is a bad thing.
How am I supposed to care about the same timeless world that sodomized me and left me catatonic on top of a roof, staring down with widened eyes at a puddle of my semen?
I’m not. That’s ridiculous. All of this is ridiculous. And now Tsuneyo is getting roped into it again just so she can be purged in another couple months after getting all of our hopes up.
But hey, maybe this can finally be the opening I need to shove my dick inside of her next and knock another off the list.
If she’s lucky, maybe she’ll disappear too and get sent back to a time before she ever met me. That’s how I’ll rationalize this. That’ll make this work for everyone.

Or maybe she’ll get even luckier and start from the beginning — trapped inside the confines of that dingy fucking ramen shop, where she will both live and die without ever experiencing life outside the walls.
I think we all need something like that.
A forceful reminder that each day is just a bridge between then and now- and that the future we all look forward to never actually comes. All we’ll get is one more unfortunate present.
And all I’ll get is tired.
: Sorry I’m late. I always wind up getting lost whenever I’m over here.
: Yeah...that’s kind of a thing she’s been doing lately.
: Any time I want to talk about world stuff, she just shrugs it off and says she doesn’t want to be bothered. And it’s really starting to get on my nerves since it’s, like...
: It’s like she’s treating this like a game.
: That’s it? I figured you’d sound a little more disappointed.
: It’s not worth it. And, honestly, not getting involved is probably better for her. It’ll save her the anguish of her expectations being repeatedly brutalized before her very eyes.
: Sensei...come on...we need to work together during times like this.
: It’s what she would have wanted.
: Are we thinking of the same person? Because the person I’m thinking of absolutely would not have wanted that. She was rooting for you to disappear the entire time. You know that.
: I know that she said that. And, call me an optimist, but I like to think she didn’t actually feel that way. She wanted to solve this more than anyone.
: And now that she’s gone you’re going to fill her shoes? Is that what this is?
: Because I’m mad, Ayane. I’m so tired of this already and I’ve only been doing it for a fraction of the time that she did. I just want it to end.
: If you wanted it to end, you wouldn’t have asked me to come to Tojo Ramen in the middle of the night just so we could talk to Tsuneyo together.
: I get that things are hard right now. They’re hard for me too. But it’s both a blessing and a curse that we have what is theoretically forever to get over that.
: That’s not a luxury we’re supposed to have. And all dwelling on the negatives will do is create a situation where it feels like you’re stuck in quicksand.
: That’s not a good analogy. You have to stop struggling to get out of quicksand. Fighting back against it will just kill you faster.
: Well, the way I see it, you’re the one who’s fighting back right now. You’re struggling harder than anyone.
: This is a mental battle, not a physical one. And if you’re spending weeks at a time internally screaming at yourself, you’re going to get killed. Not me.
: So take a deep breath, okay?...
: We’ll get through this together. You...me...Makoto...and maybe even Tsuneyo.
: I’m just tired of getting my hopes up, Ayane. I’m so tired. I’m hanging on by a thread right now.
: Well, you’re in luck. Because I just-so-happen to know how to sew. And there’s no way I’m letting you disappear on me when you’re all I have left now. Got it?
: Sure. But do you mind if I get something to eat first? I’m kind of craving ramen right now.
: Welcome to Tojo Ramen. Please take-
: Hey, Tsuneyo. Sensei gave me the run-down about your theme park reunion thingy. Is now a good time to...you know...talk about that?
: I expected three people. What has become of the class president?
: Makoto couldn’t get out of work tonight, but you don’t need to worry about her.
: You look...better than you did when we left off last night.
: I’ve had time to evaluate the situation and am now raring to go and ready to learn more. But before that, I must apologize for raising my voice at you.
: That was very impolite of me, and I am prepared to sever my pinkie-finger as penance for my actions.
: Thanks. I’ll take the one on your dominant hand.
: No, it will not be done! What’s wrong with you two?!
: If we are going to list our problems, I recommend that we start with him. His flaws are much more glaringly obvious than mine and can likely be rattled off in a matter of minutes.
: If I’m going to start, I’d like to admit right out of the gate that I’ve been the end of at least ten pay-it-forward chains this year alone.
: My turn. I personally believe that capital punishment is justified for those who leave a restaurant without finishing a dish. I’ve been told by some that this can be considered a character flaw.
: Ayane’s biggest flaw is that she’s too detail-oriented and caring.
: Why did you have to pick out the flaws that make me sound like I’m in a job interview?
: At the risk of the introductory portion of this conversation dragging on any longer, may I ask if you two will be eating or drinking anything tonight? I personally recommend the “everything.”
: The everything? Is that some kind of special?

: I think I’m okay actually. Ordering anything will just force even more time between you knowing the secrets of the universe and you not knowing the secrets of the universe. And none of us want that.
: I can not wait to sell this information to the highest bidder and use the profits to purchase a larger ramen shop.
: Unfortunately, anyone you try to reveal these secrets to will probably just interrupt you. And, on the off chance they don’t, they’ll think you’re either insane or trying to scam them.
: That sounds like an inconvenience. I hereby relinquish my powers as the world’s first backwards soothsayer.
: Someone who can see the past.
: Okay, well...considering this is the one scenario where having memories kind of is a superpower, I’ll let you keep your hero name.
: But only after listening to your “hero orientation” so your powers don’t, like...spiral out of control or something.
: So...buckle yourself in, Memory Girl. You’re in for a pretty intense info-dump.
: Do you? Because you were really silent through that entire speech and I kind of figured you’d have, like...any amount of questions about the fact that we’re in an infinitely repeating school year.
: In her defense, she’s heard this all before at that sleepover we had.
: Yes, but she doesn’t have any memories of that sleepover, so that shouldn’t be relevant.
: I am Memory Girl. I have memories of everything.
: I remember that sleepover well. I was just unaware that it was actually a memory until I learned that these “visions” were not simply visions at all.
: And I have to say I am thankful for this as I was beginning to worry that I was just having very strange and specific fantasies.
: Do you remember how that sleepover ended, though? Because I’m pretty sure that’s when one of the resets started.
: I’m not quite sure. The memories don’t appear in order. They come and go, like the Produce Delivery Administration on Tuesday, Thursday, and Sunday.
: Tsuneyo left halfway through, didn’t she?
: Yeah...I remember her getting a phone call and then disappearing.
: Do you remember anything like that, Tsuneyo? Not that it would definitely be relevant, but it might help us establish some sort of timeline.
: I apologize, but I’m unable to recall anything at this moment in time. I will remain vigilant in hopes that a new memory will approach, though.
: Nothing from the past can escape the mind of Memory Girl.
: Do you remember who else was at the sleepover, Tsuneyo? Not counting anyone shorter than me because that’s a subject Sensei isn’t ready to approach yet.
: No, it’s definitely Yumi. Because Yumi was there. She doesn’t have any recollection of it like you do, though. So I wonder what it is that makes you different?
: There is only one explanation — gluten.
: This is why they have been removing it from so many things. No one understood its powers until now. How could we have been so blind?
: We’ve finally figured it out, Ayane. You were right. All we needed to do was work together.
: You don’t think the old district has something to do with it, does it?
: What would the old district have to do with it?
: I’m trying to think of things the two of them have in common. And both of them are from the old district, aren’t they?

: Yeah...but so is Chika, and she hasn’t been involved in any of this yet. Which is great, because if I have to try explaining this to her little sister, I’m going to shoot myself with one of your guns.
: Yeah, that’s a good point. I wasn’t thinking of anyone else yet, just what Yumi and Tsuneyo share. But I think I’m at a dead end because the only other thing I can think of is D-Cups.
: Who gave you permission to violate me in my own restaurant?
: Can you think of anything else, Tsuneyo? I’m just trying to figure out what we’re supposed to do next.
: Because my instinct is saying to go back to Yumi, but I also don’t want to just go around in circles and wind up right back at the beginning the next time there's an apocalypse.
: It all comes back to gluten.
: Tsuneyo, I really don’t think it’s gluten.
: It has to be. I watched her eat my noodles with her very mouth. There is no other explanation.
: What do you think, Sensei? Should we try talking to Yumi again?
: I don’t know, Ayane. I saw Yumi the other night and-
: Tsuneyo, didn’t you talk to Yumi about this already?
: When I last saw Yumi, she said she came here to eat dinner and that you started asking her a bunch of questions.
: I ask many people many questions. It is part of my job as the Memory Ramen Girl.
: No, like weird questions. Specifically about...dates and sleepovers and things like that. She compared you to me- and said you weren’t acting like yourself.
: She does not know me very well, nor do I know her. The probability of her understanding what is or isn’t normal for me seems unlikely. Perhaps she is mistaken?
: Yumi was comparing her to you? That’s weird.
: Specifically me when I’ve “lost it.” Yumi’s around for that a lot. She’s always snapping me out of memory-lapses and blackouts and whatnot.
: How...often does that happen to you, exactly?
: A lot, but...come to think of it, you’re rarely even around when that happens, are you?
: I’m there for when you’re broken during resets, but-
: Attention, diners. I have an announcement to make.
why is it always behind you
: But on the bright side, at least Tsuneyo-
: Tsuneyo isn’t here! This is weird, right?! She was there a second ago and now she’s gone!
: Is it happening again right now?! Is it already time for the next reset?! How are we still together?! What’s going on?!
: Ayane...it’s okay. She probably just stepped outside without us noticing.  Tsuneyo’s weird. And this is a weird place.
: Why don’t we go out there and check?
: Now, quit being such a scaredy cat.
: Sensei, wait! Don’t leave without me!
i think we should stop coming here.

: On these is the wrath of God, and they shall have a grievous chastisement.

: We should probably bring her back inside now, shouldn’t we?...

: Tsuneyo, I know you probably can’t hear me on account of how nothing that happens ever makes sense anymore, but it’s probably not the best idea to wander around naked in a neighborhood full of homeless people.
: There are clues in a house near a lake. It started before you were born.
: Sensei, Tsuneyo’s pupils are, like...completely gone.
: On these is the wrath of God, and they shall have a grievous chastisement.
: Can you help me, please? I can’t move her on my own.
Ayane and I escort a naked, murderous and pupil-less Tsuneyo back inside of a blacked out ramen shop.
But the craziest part is that isn’t even the weirdest thing that happens to me tonight.
On the way home, I piss myself.
Guess it looks like I’m pee boy after all =/
What? Why? She wasn’t even here.
She masturbated to you again while all that shit was going down. I figured I’d let you know afterward so it didn’t interrupt the event.
Seriously, though. Let’s not go to the old district anymore. Just let Memory Girl’s brain get wiped again.
That girl needs a new hobby.
